Sharing a folder or a website

One command puts something in your pen under its own name, with HTTPS. Everyone in the pen can open it; nobody outside can find it.

$ ./hogman-join share photos ~/holiday

• Adding a server for photos.smith.hogman to your devices (alice)
• Sharing the folder ~/holiday as https://photos.smith.hogman

✓ https://photos.smith.hogman is up.
  Everyone in the pen can open it.
  It shows the folder ~/holiday.
  Take it down and give the name back: hogman-join share stop photos
What you can share · Keeping it running · Listing and stopping · From a computer not in the pen · Names · How it works · Limits

What you can share

CommandShares
share notes ./siteA folder, served as a website. An index.html is the front page; otherwise visitors get a file list. Links pointing outside the folder are refused.
share blog 3000Whatever is listening on port 3000 of this computer: a dev server, a self-hosted app, anything that speaks HTTP.
share nas http://192.168.1.20:8080A web address this computer can reach, such as a device on your home network. Only do this for something you mean the whole pen to reach.

For a port or address, visitors' requests are passed on with the usual X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers, and with the Host header your app expects (its own), so dev servers that check the Host header still work. WebSockets work.

Keeping it running

By default a share runs in your terminal until you press Ctrl-C. The name stays yours: run the same command later to bring it back at the same address.

To keep it running after you close the window, add --background:

$ ./hogman-join share blog 3000 --background

It runs until the computer restarts. (Starting by itself after a restart isn't built yet; run the command again.)

Listing and stopping

$ ./hogman-join share list
https://blog.smith.hogman                http://127.0.0.1:3000  (running in the background)

$ ./hogman-join share stop blog
✓ https://blog.smith.hogman is down, and the name is free again.

share stop stops it, gives the name back and removes its server from your devices. Leaving the pen (hogman-join leave) stops all of this computer's shares first. If you're in more than one pen, pick one with --pen smith.hogman.

From a computer that isn't in the pen

A spare box in the closet doesn't need to join first. On your home page, press Add a server, copy the link, and add it to the end of the command on that box (download hogman-join there the same way you did when you joined):

$ ./hogman-join share web 8080 'https://smith.pens.hogman.network/join#k=…&fp=…'

The link works once and expires in an hour. Use a server link, not an invite: an invite makes a new member.

Names

  • The name becomes https://NAME.<pen>.hogman: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. A dotted name like photos.blog works if blog is already yours and points at the same share.
  • Names are first come, first served. If it's taken, you're told and nothing is left behind; pick another.
  • Each member can hold up to 50 names.

How it works

Each share is a small device of its own: a server, joined to the pen from inside the join tool with Tailscale's tsnet. Without a link, the tool asks the pen (as you, through your computer's existing connection) for a one-time server key. The share then:

  1. joins the mesh as a server, so members may connect to it;
  2. claims its name (a server may only name itself, with a free name or one already pointing at it);
  3. gets a 7-day certificate from the pen's CA over ACME and renews it on its own;
  4. listens on the mesh at ports 443 and 80 (80 redirects to HTTPS) and serves the folder or passes visitors to your port.

Your laptop itself stays a personal device that accepts no connections. Nothing opens a port on your computer, and nothing needs administrator rights. Its state lives in your user config folder under hogman-shares/<pen>/<name>.

Limits

  • Shares don't come back by themselves after a restart yet.
  • A computer that joined as a server can't share without a server link (servers can't add devices).
  • Windows is untested.
  • For a permanent site with its own web server configuration, see Running a server.

Something wrong or unclear on this page? Its source is in site/docs-src; issues and fixes welcome.
